THE AUDITOR'S HALF IS A SEPARATE AUTHORITY AND THE MODULE SAYS WHY, in three reasons that are this theorem's premise: a chain is not whole until its last hop, so a PEP attesting per hop could only ever commit to a truncated record; the audit posture is the auditor's to choose; and registering against a transparency service is network I/O, which in front of a response would make an audit dependency an availability dependency.

THE EVIDENCE ALREADY EXISTED. This is an OWNERSHIP gap, not an evidence gap — attest_chain has three controls in transparency_e2e_test.rs and no unit cited any of them. The third is the one R9-C103/C128 exist for: the self-check used to be SKIPPED for a reconstruction that broke at hop 0, on the reasoning that such a record names no call. That is right about the identity fields and wrong about the submission, which is call-specific there too — so the one check that could catch a statement issued over different bytes was absent on exactly the records an auditor investigates.

WHAT COMES BACK IS BOTH, AND THAT IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE CLAIM. A SignedStatement alone does not say whether the record it describes is whole; the ChainLabel inside it does. Returning only the statement would leave a caller acting on an INCOMPLETE verdict, or discovering it by decoding a document it had already submitted — at which point it is public. BoundToSubmissionOnly is carried rather than collapsed into success for the same reason.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing about the serving path, which retains and does nothing else; not that the chain is complete or that its hops verify, only that the label reaches the caller; nothing about the transparency service, its registration or its receipt; and no custody claim about the issuing key, which arrives as a caller-supplied closure.
